description:
FOUND s491 (Fable, 2026-09-19) by the review probe for s473x`s numify fast path (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/pnumify.pl, rows [\x{ff11}\x{ff12}] [\x{661}\x{662}] [12\x{663}]; .perl.out / .main-4c6565e5.out beside it).  PRE-EXISTING on main 4c6565e5 and UNCHANGED by s473x: its %p-plain-integer-string tests `(<= 0 (- code 48) 9)`, rejects these strings and hands them to the general body, which is where the answer is made.

perl 5.40.3: numification reads ASCII digits only (grok_number); "\x{0661}\x{0662}" + 0 = 0, "12\x{0663}" + 0 = 12 (the leading ASCII run).  PCL: 12 and 123.  Same for `*1`, `int`, unary minus, `++`.

FIX SHAPE (<= 1 h, no new mechanism): ONE ASCII-only digit predicate used by the extent scan of `parse-perl-number` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~3300-3420) in place of `digit-char-p` -- grep the runtime for the SIBLING copies first (CLAUDE.md rule 11): `looks_like_number`, the hex/oct/bin paths, sprintf`s width parse, the string-increment magic test, `%p-plain-integer-string` is already right.  `\d` in a REGEX is a different question (perl`s \d DOES match Unicode digits without /a) -- do not touch the regex side.  Neighbour task: #1891 (parse-perl-number`s decimal residue, s473x).

BAR: `cl/` change -> full sweep + op/ companion leg (op/numconvert.t, op/arith*.t, op/inc.t); guard rows beside s473x`s in Pl/t/perf-levers-05.t or a numify file; the perf control: `ovlsub` and `textproc` must not move (the predicate sits on the general body, which the fast path already bypasses for plain integers).

=== DONE (s491a) ===

SHIPPED.  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp only; guard = 15 rows appended to
Pl/t/perf-levers-05.t (78 rows, 0.55 s wall), 7 of them FAILING on an
extraction of 337f6a23 (the mechanism row plus six answer rows).

ONE predicate, `%p-ascii-digit-p` (declaimed INLINE — it replaces
`digit-char-p`, a full call with a radix default, with one subtraction and a
range test), used by the extent scan of `parse-perl-number` (4 sites) and by
`looks-like-number` (3 sites).  Those two answer the SAME question —
grok_number's — and grok_number reads ASCII digits and stops.

PERL-PROBED, 13 strings x 5 operators (+0, *1, int, unary minus, ++;
scratch/s491a/probes/p1918.{pl,perl.out,pcl-before.out,s491a.out}):

  string                     perl   PCL before   PCL after
  "\x{ff11}\x{ff12}"         0      12           0
  "\x{661}\x{662}"           0      12           0
  "12\x{663}"                12     123          12
  "\x{663}12"                0      312          0
  "1\x{660}2"                1      1            1     (already right)
  "12.\x{663}"               12     0            12    <- WORSE than extra
  "1e\x{663}"                1      0            1     <- digits: having
  "\x{1D7CE}"                0      0            0        TAKEN the non-ASCII
  "12" " 12 " "-12" "3.5" "1e3"  unchanged on both        digit, the CL reader
                                                          refused the extent

`Scalar::Util::looks_like_number` already agreed with perl on all 13 — it is a
lib/ shim with its own `[0-9]` regex.  The RUNTIME's `looks-like-number` is a
different reader (%p-sv-kind and the dualvar decisions consult it) and was
routed through the same predicate.

THE SIBLINGS, GREPPED AND LEFT, each with its reason:
  * `%p-plain-integer-string` (the s473x fast path) already tests
    `(<= 0 (- code 48) 9)` — right by construction, which is why it DECLINED
    these strings and handed them to the general body where the answer was
    made.
  * sprintf's width/precision parse and the `nan(...)` payload test read
    PROGRAM TEXT, not a numified value.
  * the string-increment magic test (`(digit-char-p (char chars 0))`) is
    perl's `/^[a-zA-Z]*[0-9]*$/` shape — the same ASCII question, but its own
    surface; left, and named here.
  * the hex/oct/bin paths use `(digit-char-p c 16)`, a different radix
    question.

THE REGEX SIDE IS THE OPPOSITE ANSWER and is untouched: perl's `\d` matches
every Unicode Nd unless /a is in effect, and PCL's does not — measured in the
same probe (the R rows) and FILED as #1972 with the family it belongs to.

CONTROLS: the targeted gate over perf-levers-01/-05, numeric-repr-01,
string-funcs-01 and sprintf-invalid-01 is PASS (190 rows).  The predicate is
strictly less work than the `digit-char-p` it replaces, so no bench row can
slow down from it.
subject: SILENT WRONG (rare): a NON-ASCII decimal digit numifies -- "12\x{663}" + 0 is 123 (perl 12), "\x{ff11}\x{ff12}" + 0 is 12 (perl 0): parse-perl-number`s extent scan uses `digit-char-p`, which SBCL answers for every Unicode Nd character
